repos.name: codejson-schemas
repos.description: code.json: A metadata standard for federal software projects

items: `identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`$id` updated to `https://gsa-share-it.github.io/code-json-schema.json` (reflecting the repository's move from the `DSACMS` org to `GSA-SHARE-IT`).
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
`identifier` added to `required`.
`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, `date`, `description`, `laborHours`, `languages`, `tags`, and `vcs` removed from `required` (now optional).
`feedbackMechanism` (singular)

`version`, `homepageURL`, `downloadURL`, `disclaimerURL`, `disclaimerText`, `relatedCode`, `reusedCode`, `partners` added as optional fields, taken from original [M-16-21 code.json schema](https://github.com/GSA/code-gov-data/tree/master/schemas)
`AIUseCaseID` added for assisting with agency collection of their AI Use Case Inventory as part of M-25-21 compliance
`SBOM` added to include software's SBOM in metadata as part of EO 14028

`categories`, `feedbackMechanisms` (plural, replaced by singular `feedbackMechanism`), `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, `softwareType` — these agency-extension-style fields were dropped from the generic gov-wide schema.
Migrated `$schema` dialect from `draft-04` to `2020-12` and introduced a formal `$id` (`https://dsacms.github.io/code-json-schema.json`).

Corrected the same structural bug present in `gov-schema-1.0.0.json`, where all field definitions were incorrectly nested one level too deep under a top-level `items` key instead of directly under `properties`.
`permissions.usageType` changed from a single `string` value to an `array` of strings, allowing multiple exemption reasons to be declared simultaneously.

Expanded and refined the exemption enum taxonomy: the old `exemptByLaw` was split into `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByNationalIntelligence`, `exemptByFOIA`, `exemptByEAR`, `exemptByITAR`, `exemptByTSA`, and `exemptByClassifiedInformation`; the old `exemptByNationalSecurity` (covering national security, confidentiality, _and_ individual privacy risk) was split so privacy risk became its own value, `exemptByPrivacyRisk`; `exemptByIPRestriction` was also added.

`organization`: removed the CMS-specific enum restriction (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`) and generalized it to a free-text string with an example (`'18F'` or `'Navy'`) suitable for any agency.
Top-level `additionalProperties` changed from `false` to `true`, allowing agencies to extend the schema with their own custom fields.

`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, and `feedbackMechanism` added to `required`; `categories`, `feedbackMechanisms`, `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, and `softwareType` removed from `required` (dropped entirely, see Removed above).
Field definitions are nested one level too deep under `properties.items` instead of directly under `properties` (the same structural bug present in the CMS schema's `schema-0.0.0.json`).

`permissions.usageType` is a single `string` value (not an array), so only one exemption reason could be declared per release, with a smaller 8-value exemption enum (`openSource`, `governmentWideReuse`, `exemptByLaw`, `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, `exemptByPolicyDate`).
`organization` was restricted to a CMS-only enum value (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`), despite this being the generic, agency-agnostic schema.
`identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
Updated the `usageType` description text to define and renumber all 13 enum values to match.

Reworded the `reuseFrequency` description for clarity: _"Measures frequency of code reuse in various forms such as forks and clones for repositories, and downloads for packaged and distributed software."_

commits.message:
fix: TRB assign lead modal submit not firing

The Submit button had `data-close-modal`, so one click both ran
handleSubmit and closed the modal. Closing added `is-hidden`, which
triggered the MutationObserver's `reset()` while handleSubmit was still
validating, so the submit callback sometimes never ran and the mutation
was never sent.

- Remove `data-close-modal` from the Submit button

commits.message:
feat(misc#420): check the pr-env reaper token before reaping and warn ahead of its expiry (#650)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#420

## What

The reaper files its tracking issue with `PR_ENV_REAPER_TOKEN`, the same
token it reaps with. When that token expires, Reap fails on its first
`gh api` call and Report fails on `gh issue list`, so nobody hears about
it. This adds a preflight that checks the token first and warns before
it expires, while the token can still post the warning.

- New `scripts/pr-env-token-preflight.sh`, run as the first step after
checkout. It calls `gh api repos/CMS-Enterprise/<repo>` for ztmf,
ztmf-ui and ztmf-misc. Any refusal prints a `::error::` naming the repo,
and the step fails once all three are checked. The refusal also goes in
the report, so the tracking issue names the repo when the token can
still post there.
- It reads the token's expiry from the
`github-authentication-token-expiration` header and logs it on every
run. Within `TOKEN_WARN_DAYS` (14, set in the workflow env) it writes a
warning naming the date and the secret.
- The Report step puts that text at the top of its report and uses the
same lookup as before: comment on the open tracking issue, or open one.
A dry run only writes the summary, as before. The run goes on to reap
after a warning.
- No expiry header means the token has no expiry date. That logs a
`::warning::` and passes. A header that does not parse is reported to
the tracking issue with the raw value, so someone checks it by hand.

## Limits

ztmf and ztmf-ui are public, so `GET repos/X` succeeds for any valid
token, even one not granted that repo. For those two, the preflight
catches a token that is expired or revoked, but not one that lost access
to the repo. ztmf-misc is internal, so its check is complete. A token
missing a repo still fails at Reap and shows up through Report.

A network error or a 5xx on any of the three calls fails the preflight
and skips that night's reap. Before this change, Reap would have failed
on its own first `gh` call in the same case.

Inside the 14-day window the warning posts every night, the same way
findings do.

## How I tested it

There is no test setup for the workflow scripts, so I ran the preflight,
Reap and Report steps from this file in job order. I used stand-in `gh`
and `aws` commands on `PATH`, GNU `date`, and the real
`pr-env-reaper.sh`.

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Expiry 60 days out | Passes, logs the date, clean run |
| Expiry 10 days out, tracking issue open | Comments on that issue with
the date and secret; reap still runs |
| Expiry 10 days out, no issue open | Opens the tracking issue with the
warning |
| ztmf-ui refuses the token | `::error::PR_ENV_REAPER_TOKEN was refused
by CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui: ...`, step fails, Report's comment names the
refusal and the failed run |
| Token expired (401 everywhere) | One `::error::` per repo |
| No expiry header | Warning in the log, passes |
| Header does not parse | Reported to the tracking issue, reap still
runs |
| 14 days minus/plus an hour | Warns / does not |
| Dry run inside the window | Warning in the summary only, no issue
calls |

actionlint is clean on the workflow, and shellcheck 0.11.0 is clean on
the script.

After merge: a `dry_run` dispatch shows the expiry date in the log.
Seeing the comment on the tracking issue needs a run that is not a dry
run inside the window, which the first scheduled run after 2026-12-13
will be. The token expires 2026-12-27.

commits.message:
fix(misc#415, misc#416): skip fork PRs and publish main's test image in order (#652)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#415

Also the ztmf half of
[ztmf-misc#416](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc/issues/416).
Its ztmf-ui half, the same change on the `ztmf_ui_tag` publish, is
[ui!779](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui/pull/779). I'll close
ztmf-misc#416 by hand once both have merged.

## What and why

Two follow-ups from Mack's review of
[ztmf!593](https://github.com/CMS-Enterprise/ztmf/pull/593), both in
`.github/workflows/orchestration-pr.yml`.

**Skip fork PRs (ztmf-misc#415).** A run from a fork PR gets no repo
secrets, so `PR_ENV_ROLEARN` is empty. On open, "Build PR API image"
fails. On close, the teardown and its failure comment both fail. A
merged fork PR fails `publish-main`. `build`, `teardown` and
`publish-main` now require
`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`,
next to the Dependabot exclusions. `deploy` needs no change because it
only runs after `build`. A PR from a fork that has since been deleted
has no head repo, so it is skipped too. The header comment now covers
forks. A fork PR that needs an environment gets rehomed to an in-repo
branch, as before. ztmf-ui's workflow already has this guard.

**Publish `ztmf_api_test_tag` in merge order (ztmf-misc#416).** The
workflow-level concurrency group is per PR, so merges of two PRs ran
`publish-main` side by side, and whichever finished last wrote the tag.
There are three changes to `publish-main`:

- It gets its own job-level group shared across PRs
(`publish-main-ztmf`, `cancel-in-progress: false`), so publishes run one
at a time.
- It builds main's tip instead of the PR's merge commit. A run that
joins the group cancels the one already waiting, and "newer" there means
the run that arrived later, not the later merge: a merged PR whose close
run sat behind its own in-flight deploy can arrive late and cancel a
newer merge's waiting run. Building main's tip makes that harmless,
since every run publishes everything merged before it started. It also
means a merged fork PR, which skips this job, is picked up by the next
publish.
- The write only moves the tag forward. Before `put-parameter`, the step
reads the current `ztmf_api_test_tag` and compares that commit to the
one it built through the compare API. If the recorded commit is the same
or newer (`identical` or `behind`), it leaves the tag alone with a
notice. A missing parameter or a failed compare still writes.

## Change from the ticket

ztmf-misc#416 asked to compare the merge commit to main's head and skip
the write if main had moved on. Building main's tip makes that
comparison always pass, so it is replaced by the forward-only check. A
head-of-main skip on its own would also leave the tag stale whenever the
newer merge does not publish: a Dependabot merge, a fork PR, a failed
run, or a cancelled waiting run.

## Behavior changes

- A fork PR shows the three jobs as skipped, not failed, on open and on
close, and no teardown failure comment is posted.
- `ztmf_api_test_tag` now names main's tip when the publish ran, which
can be later than the PR that triggered it.
- When merges queue up, a waiting `publish-main` run is cancelled by the
next one to arrive, so a merged PR can show that job as cancelled. The
later run includes its merge.
- A run that would move the tag backward logs a notice and does not
write it.

## Verification

- `actionlint`: the only finding is SC2129 on the `deploy` job's
Terraform apply step, which is already on main.
- The compare-and-skip logic, run against real commits on main: recorded
older writes (`ahead`), recorded newer skips (`behind`), same commit
skips (`identical`), an unknown commit writes, and a missing parameter
writes.
- `make test-unit`, `make test-integration` and `make test-e2e` (327
ran, 0 failed) pass. None of them exercise workflows, but they are the
gate.
- The ticket's two-merges-back-to-back check can only run after this
merges. The next pair of merges should show the second `publish-main`
waiting on the first, and the tag at the later merge's `main-<sha>`.

commits.message:
Migrate ScoreDiffModal onto queries and delete its cache (#770)

* refactor(misc#362): read the score diff through a query

The comparison fetched its diff with a .then/.catch/.finally chain and its
own AbortController, and held the rows, the spinner and the error in three
useStates. A query on the existing scores.diff key replaces all of it, and
the request is skipped until both ends are chosen and they differ.

diffKey is gone with it. That counter was bumped on open purely to force the
effect to re-run, which made every reopen refetch. A diff only changes when
an answer does, and an answer write already invalidates the whole scores
prefix, so reopening now serves the cached rows. A reopen after a failure
still retries, because the modal has no other retry control and a transient
failure would otherwise stick until the pickers changed.

The old catch set the same inline message whether or not isAuthHandled was
true, so an auth failure that had already toasted reported twice. The query
suppresses the cache-boundary snackbar and the modal keeps its own alert.

Adding the first query hook to this modal left its suite, and the Pillar
Scores suite that renders it, without a QueryClientProvider.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#362

* refactor(misc#362): read the data calls through the shared hook

The last of the epic's three hand-written caches. The modal kept its own
module-level datacallsCache behind a ten-minute TTL, sorted the response
itself, and fetched on every open that fell outside the window.

useDatacalls reads the same endpoint and does the same deadline sort in
select, so the effect collapses to the default-selection logic. The layout
reads that key for the whole session, which means opening the modal is a
cache hit and the entry never loses its observer. That is what makes
deleting the cache safe rather than merely tidy: a module-level singleton
survived unmount, and the gcTime the TTL maps onto would not have.

Seeding is keyed on the opening rather than run on every list change, since
a shared list can refetch while the modal is open and would otherwise throw
away whatever the user had picked. The wait now covers seeding too: the code
this replaces set the list and the defaults in one batch, so the pickers
never rendered empty, and reading the list from a query splits that into two
renders.

The suite's Date.now mock went with the cache; it existed only to wind the
clock past that TTL between tests.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#362

* fix(misc#362): gate the score diff on open and skip the 403 snackbar

Both callers keep the dialog mounted, so an ungated diff query kept
observing after close: it refetched on answer writes and never read the
server again on reopen. Passing enabled: open fixes both and lets the
wasOpen retry effect go.

The diff request now sends skipPermissionNotification, so a 403 shows
only the inline alert instead of the interceptor snackbar as well.

Also updates the ScoreDiffModal doc and two stale comments.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#362

* test(misc#362): refetch the diff on reopen after an answer write

Extends the closed-modal test so it also reopens and asserts a second
/scores/diff request, pinning the half that only a manual check covered.
